Title: Optimising spare parts management in hydraulic excavators: a Fuzzy CODAS and ABC analysis approach
Authors: Isik Ates Kiral, Zehra Ilke Erdem, Emre Cakmak, Sevilay Demirkesen
Affiliations: Bursa Technical University; Piri Reis University; Istinye University; Gebze Technical University
Abstract: The reliable operation of heavy construction equipment is critical for project productivity; however, spare parts inventory decisions for such equipment are often made using intuition-based or oversimplified approaches, leading to unnecessary costs and equipment downtime. In particular, construction-specific spare parts management lacks systematic, data-driven frameworks that account for uncertainty, multiple decision criteria, and operational criticality. To address this gap, this study proposes a hybrid decision-support framework that integrates Fuzzy Combinative Distance-Based Assessment (Fuzzy CODAS) with Always Better Control (ABC) analysis to optimise spare parts inventory for hydraulic excavators. The framework is applied to the hydraulic system of excavators using 22 spare parts and 13 evaluation criteria assessed by industry experts. The results indicate that pump devices, gear pumps, and regulator pumps should be prioritised as Class A items due to their high criticality, cost impact, and failure consequences, while components such as cylinders, centre joints, and certain piping systems exhibit lower stocking priority. The findings demonstrate that component-specific inventory strategies can significantly reduce operational costs and improve equipment uptime. Theoretically, this study advances spare parts management literature by introducing a construction-oriented hybrid MCDM framework, while providing an evidence-based tool for strategic inventory planning and maintenance decision-making in heavy equipment operations.

Title: Can the use of recycled powders reduce AM spare parts costs?
Authors: Mirco Peron, Luigi Panza, Mohammad Arbabian
Affiliations: NEOMA Business School; Politecnico di Torino; University of Portland
Abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) has attracted growing interest for spare parts production, yet its industrial adoption remains limited. A key barrier is cost, particularly the high cost of raw materials. Prior research suggests that replacing virgin powders with recycled powders could significantly reduce material costs. Recycled powders also offer environmental benefits which, under carbon reduction policies, may translate into additional economic savings. However, these advantages are offset by drawbacks: recycled powders typically exhibit lower quality, leading to reduced part reliability and higher spare parts management costs. This trade-off raises a critical question: does the use of recycled powders reduce AM spare parts costs, as suggested by the literature? Through analytical and numerical analyses supported by a case study, we show that this is only conditionally true. While recycled powders can lower total costs, their economic viability depends on the balance between material cost savings, reliability degradation, and carbon pricing. We identify threshold regions that distinguish scenarios in which recycled powders are always, never, or only conditionally preferable. Results indicate that the threshold regions are up to twice as sensitive to changes in reliability as to changes in material cost, while carbon pricing and emission reductions have only a marginal effect.

Title: A constraint programming-based decomposition procedure for shop scheduling problems
Authors: Francisco Yuraszeck, Gonzalo Mejía, Daniel Alejandro Rossit, Armin Lüer-Villagra
Affiliations: Universidad Andres Bello; Universidad de La Sabana; Universidad Nacional del Sur (UNS); INMABB, Universidad Nacional del Sur (UNS)-CONICET
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a two-phase constraint programming (CP) based algorithm to obtain high-quality lower and upper bounds for classical scheduling problems under the makespan minimisation criterion. The method relies on a resource-constrained project scheduling problem (RCPSP) formulation that incorporates a decomposition approach and a warm-start mechanism exploiting the problem structure to derive competitive bounds. We evaluate our approach on 280 instances of the non-permutation flow shop scheduling problem (NPFSSP) and the job shop scheduling problem (JSSP), comprising 120 and 160 instances, respectively. A comprehensive computational analysis shows that the proposed decomposition approach (DA) is highly competitive in terms of optimality gap and relative percentage deviation with respect to both the lower and upper bounds, outperforming a direct solution (DS) approach commonly used in industrial practice. DA consistently dominates DS across most instance subsets, both in average performance and in variability. We further validate our approach on 20 real-world industrial instances featuring non-rectangular job structures, job recirculation, and unbalanced machine workloads, reaching the optimal makespan on all instances in an average of 251 s. By obtaining highly competitive bounds, our proposed decomposition procedure increases managerial confidence when committing to due dates, allocating workloads, or evaluating whether additional capacity is required.

Title: Lagrangian framework fusion with deep learning for steelmaking-continuous casting scheduling
Authors: Liyi Yu, Xirang Hao, Liangliang Sun, Zhenghao Song, Mengshuang Li, Yunpeng Li, Natalia M. Matsveichuk, Yuri N. Sotskov
Affiliations: Northeastern University; Belarusian State Agrarian Technical University; National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
Abstract: Steelmaking–continuous casting (SCC) production scheduling is a critical step for optimising charge combinations, enhancing process compactness, and reducing energy consumption, thereby influencing the production efficiency and economic benefits of steel enterprises. However, the small batch sizes and extensive product variety inherent in modern steelmaking substantially increase scheduling complexity, making it difficult to rapidly generate feasible production plans. Therefore, we incorporate deep learning (DL) into the surrogate Lagrangian relaxation (SLR) framework to accelerate the acquisition of scheduling schemes by replacing the costly process of accurately solving subproblems with predicting ‘good-enough’ subproblem solutions. First, we propose a novel pointer network (GDPN) that integrates gated recurrent unit (GRU) with dot-product attention (DPA) to predict subproblem solutions in the Lagrange decomposition-coordination process. Subsequently, a dual-phase masking (DM) mechanism is developed during both the training and inference of GDPN to enforce the feasibility of the surrogate subproblem constraints caused by the continuous casting process in SCC. Finally, extensive numerical experiments and an industrial study with different scales demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DM-GDPN-SLR method.

Title: A comprehensive sustainability-based framework for locating net-zero manufacturing facilities
Authors: Melike Cari, Betul Sasmazturk, Ertugrul Ayyildiz, Betul Kara
Affiliations: Karadeniz Technical University; Hasan Kalyoncu University; Industrial Policy and Development Center, Istanbul Ticaret University, Istanbul, Türkiye
Abstract: Achieving net-zero manufacturing requires robust strategies that balance environmental, economic, and operational priorities while aligning with global sustainability targets. Integrating advanced decision-making methodologies with comprehensive sustainability frameworks is crucial for guiding climate-neutral industrial transformation. This study develops a modular decision-aid model, namely the Net-Zero Manufacturing Location Decision-Aid Model, for evaluating net-zero manufacturing facility locations from a production-system and logistics-readiness perspective. The model systematically incorporates ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) and HSE (Health, Safety, Environment) criteria and operationalises them through Picture Fuzzy Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (PiF-SWARA) and Picture Fuzzy Additive Ratio Assessment (PiF-ARAS). Expert judgments are aggregated through picture fuzzy logic, capturing uncertainty and subjectivity inherent in real-world decision environments. Results demonstrate that environmental and safety dimensions are the most influential factors in site selection for net-zero manufacturing, while governance and health play a moderate role, and social criteria are relatively less impactful. Sensitivity analysis confirms the stability and robustness of the model across various weighting scenarios. The proposed framework provides actionable insights for decision-makers and policymakers aiming to enable climate-neutral manufacturing investments. This study contributes a scalable, transparent, and replicable methodology, supporting the strategic alignment of industrial development with circular economy principles and smart production technologies.

Title: Correction
Reconfiguring supply chains amid geopolitical risks: a systematic review of emerging topics
Authors: Xinyue Liu, William Ho, Hugo K.S. Lam, Srinivas Talluri
Affiliations: The University of Melbourne; University of Liverpool; Michigan State University
Abstract: In recent years, geopolitical events such as Brexit and the U.S.–China trade war have become increasingly frequent and have had significant impacts on supply chains. Supply chain reconfiguration has been recognised as an effective approach to addressing geopolitical risks (GPRs). However, existing literature reviews in this field exhibit several limitations that motivate us to advance the understanding of supply chain reconfiguration amid GPRs. Accordingly, we conduct a systematic literature review of 92 high-quality journal articles published between 2015 and May 2026 to identify key emerging topics, their antecedents–decisions–outcomes (ADO) frameworks, and the associated research gaps and future research directions. Specifically, we apply a topic modelling technique combined with a semantic validation approach to classify the articles into five topics and rank their scores of emergence. This process identifies three emerging topics: supply chain reconfigurations in advanced technology sectors, adaptive risk management approaches, and diversification strategies. For each emerging topic, we develop topic-specific research frameworks using an ADO framework incorporating moderators. Based on identified gaps, we propose tailored future research directions for each emerging topic. Overall, this study advances the understanding of supply chain reconfiguration amid GPRs and provides actionable insights for future researchers and practitioners.

Title: Enhancing supply chain resilience through green investment under emerging contaminants risk: a network game theory perspective
Authors: Daipeng Ma, Jian Guan, Rui Li, Xiaohong Chen
Affiliations: Central South University; Xiangjiang Laboratory
Abstract: As emerging contaminant risks intensify, supply chains in pollution-sensitive industries have become increasingly uncertain and vulnerable. Containing pollution risk diffusion and enhancing supply chain resilience therefore constitute urgent theoretical and practical challenges. Based on inter-firm supply and demand relationships, this study constructs a network game model incorporating firm pollution sensitivity, economic exposure, and green investment. By comparing independent firm decision-making, homogeneous decision-making with network effects, and heterogeneous decision-making, this study conducts numerical simulations using data from 391 firms across six typical pollution-sensitive industries. The findings show that complementary business relationships alter the marginal returns to firms’ green investment and may induce free-riding-like strategic dependence under network externalities, thereby weakening preventive green investment incentives and increasing supply-chain network vulnerability. Firms’ green investment decisions are jointly driven by their own pollution sensitivity, potential economic losses, and partners’ risk exposure. Supply-chain topology further moderates the green investment–resilience relationship: when cooperation is limited, higher business concentration strengthens network resilience; when cooperation is intensive but structurally imbalanced, improving the green governance capacity of vulnerable firms and reducing structural asymmetry more effectively curb pollution-risk diffusion. These findings provide implications for stakeholders’ green governance and supply chain risk management decisions.

Title: Integrated large language models and digital twin-based decision support in closed-loop supply chain operations: green steel transition case study
Authors: Chi An Le, Devika Kannan, Kannan Govindan, Truong Thinh Nguyen
Affiliations: Adelaide University
Abstract: The green steel transition requires corporates to operate closed-loop supply chains (CLSCs) that involve operational decisions under heterogeneous data. Although decision models have shifted CLSC operations towards advanced analytics and optimisation, challenges remain in automatically interpreting natural-language requests, enabling data-driven reasoning, and communicating outcomes for actionable decision-making. Motivated by recent progress in large language models (LLMs), we propose an intelligent digital twin-based decision-support method (LMiDTSC) to automatically interpret, reason, and address CLSC operational tasks, and synchronise physical and digital CLSC resources. We develop a knowledge graph, a benchmark, and an accurate query-explanation consistency (AQEC) metric to operate the method and evaluate its effectiveness in supporting decisions on steel distribution and scrap collection. Across focal operational tasks, LMiDTSC outperforms baselines (e.g. GPT-5.2) by 82.73% in AQEC, while its fine-tune outperforms backbones using proprietary models by 93.17% in AQEC. This study advances decision support systems and AI-enabled operations research by integrating LLMs and digital twins for computerised decisions in CLSC operations. This study suggests supply chain practitioners should consider high-performing LLMs for complex operational tasks and exercise caution in scaling in-context learning prompts. Finally, policymakers can accelerate the implementation of such integrated decision support systems by promoting industrial symbiosis and workforce training.

Title: Supply-demand uncertainty in bone China supply chains: distributionally robust optimization with voluntary and recycled resources
Authors: Hadi Hassanzadeh, Hossein Neghabi
Affiliations: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad
Abstract: This paper dvelops a mathematical model for designing a multi-echelon Bone China Supply Chain (BCSC), aiming to minimise total costs minus revenues through decisions related to facility location, supplier selection, and material flow quantities across the network. The model explicitly incorporates simultaneous uncertainty in both raw material supply and product demand, which is addressed using a Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) approach. Additionally, part of the required raw material is obtained through voluntarily contributed recycled sources. To solve the proposed model, we employ the L-shaped Benders decomposition algorithm and an enhanced version that incorporates a warm-up strategy to improve computational efficiency. Computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves higher profitability and better demand fulfillment rates under various uncertainty scenarios compared to traditional stochastic optimisation methods. Moreover, the inclusion of voluntary recycled inputs significantly reduces operational costs and enhances the overall economic performance of the BCSC. The results also confirm the effectiveness of the warm-up strategy in accelerating convergence and improving solution quality, particularly in large-scale instances.

Title: A review of process planning from an operations research perspective: models, algorithms, and benchmarks
Authors: Yiming Ma, Kaiping Luo, Qiuhong Zhao, Lianyu Zheng
Affiliations: Beihang University; Management and Decision (Beihang University), Ministry of Education
Abstract: Process planning bridges product design and manufacturing and increasingly involves multiple types of flexibility. As an NP-hard combinatorial optimisation problem, it poses substantial methodological challenges, yet effective optimisation is critical for improving production performance. This paper presents a review of process planning from an operations research perspective, covering models, algorithms, and benchmarks. We systematically classify mathematical programming models according to key characteristics, including model class, flexibility types, and objective settings, and highlight recent advances in linearisation techniques and compact formulations. From an algorithmic standpoint, we review and categorise solution paradigms, encompassing metaheuristics, multi-objective optimisation, deterministic methods, heuristics, and reinforcement learning, and analyse their respective strengths and limitations. In addition, we compile benchmark test cases together with technical specifications and best-known solutions to support systematic performance comparison. Finally, we identify research gaps and outline promising future directions, with particular emphasis on advanced optimisation methods and practically relevant modelling.

Title: Hierarchical collaborative scheduling in cloud manufacturing based on dynamic contract net protocol and deep reinforcement learning
Authors: Xi Wang, Yongkui Liu, Chunfu Zhong, Lihui Wang, Bin Zi, Yueqin Huo, Wenxue Wang
Affiliations: Xidian University; KTH Royal Institute of Technology; China National Heavy Machinery Research Institute Co., Ltd.; Chongqing University
Abstract: Cloud manufacturing facilitates collaborative production by integrating distributed manufacturing resources via service-oriented platforms. However, its scheduling process is constrained by resource heterogeneity, complex task dependencies, and inefficient platform-enterprise coordination. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach for multi-task scheduling that integrates a contract net protocol (CNP) with graph neural networks (GNNs). First, a platform-enterprise collaborative scheduling framework is proposed. Then, two CNP-based schemes are designed and extended into a Dynamic CNP (DCNP) which updates evaluation weights to improved service selection. Moreover, an RGCN-LDDQN algorithm is proposed, which integrates relational graph convolutional networks (RGCN), long short-term memory (LSTM), and double deep Q-network (DDQN) to model inter-task dependencies and support global scheduling decisions. A bi-level priority constraint is integrated to mitigate conflicts, and a priority-aware P-RGCN-LDDQN is obtained, which enhances feasibility and stability. Subtasks are autonomously scheduled using a genetic algorithm at the enterprise layer based on platform-issued objectives and constraints. Simulations with respect to automotive parts assembly tasks are conducted. Results indicate that, under DCNP, RGCN-LDDQN reduces makespan by 21.88% and comprehensive cost by 15.64% compared to conventional DDQN, while maintaining service quality. Additionally, P-RGCN-LDDQN achieves further reductions of 9.15% and 6.69% over RGCN-LDDQN.

Title: Collaborative negotiation and auction protocols for multi-agent supply networks
Authors: Frederik A. Weber, Shimon Y. Nof
Affiliations: Purdue University

Title: When brands go live: AI host or profit-popularity driven influencer?
Authors: Baozhuang Niu, Xingyun Yue, Fanzhuo Zeng, Nan Zhang
Affiliations: South China University of Technology; University of Southampton
Abstract: Livestreaming sales (LSS) has become one of the fastest-growing formats in digital commerce, yet rising commission rates render influencer-led livestreaming increasingly costly. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) now offer a promising alternative: AI-powered virtual hosts that engage consumers and promote products without commission payments, albeit with lower interactional efficiency. This paper examines the brand's strategic choice between influencer-led and AI-hosted LSS. We develop an analytical model involving a brand and a dual-purpose influencer who values both commission and popularity-related benefits such as follower-base expansion. Our analysis uncovers two opposing mechanisms shaping how cost dynamics affect livestreaming choices. The influencer interactional-compensation effect captures the influencer's tendency to raise interactional richness as product cost increases, thereby helping stabilise demand. In contrast, the AI price-stabilisation effect results in lower interactional investment but more stable pricing. We show that when the influencer cares only about commission earnings, AI hosting is optimal only for low-cost products. If the influencer is profit-popularity driven, however, AI hosting may remain profitable for mid-to-high-cost products when AI is inefficient and popularity incentive is strong. Our results highlight the importance of tailoring livestreaming mode with product cost structure and the moderating role of the influencer's profit-popularity motivation.

Title: Resource allocation and patient care: a two-stage network-DEA model for optimising rural hospital operations
Authors: Guilherme P. Afonso, Dinesh R. Pai, José Rui Figueira, Diogo Filipe Cunha Ferreira
Affiliations: CERIS, Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa; Penn State Harrisburg; CEGIST, Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa
Abstract: We propose an evaluation framework to enhance U.S. rural hospital efficiency and sustainability amid rising costs and staffing shortages. Moving beyond ‘black-box’ evaluations, we utilise a two-stage Network-Data Envelopment Analysis (N-DEA) Slack-Based Measure model - Resource Allocation and Patient Care Delivery – to analyse internal inefficiencies. To ensure validity, 57 rural hospitals were segmented by size. To capture performance evolution, we integrate the Hicks-Moorsteen Productivity Index to evaluate annual Total Factor Productivity (TFP) shifts. We model hospitals as production systems converting resources into health outcomes. Applied to a 2018–2023 dataset, the model reveals that Patient Care Delivery consistently outperforms Resource Allocation. Longitudinal analysis indicates that while 48 of 57 hospitals recorded net TFP increases, volatility persists, particularly among small and medium facilities. This suggests performance gains are achievable by addressing Resource Allocation bottlenecks. Slack analysis reveals divergent profiles: small hospitals frequently operate with zero slack, whereas the broader sample shows 20% average excess for physicians and certified nurse practitioners. Scenario testing confirms modest reductions (25%) in these roles would enhance efficiency by 1.8%. Conversely, we recommend protecting registered nurse staffing due to minimal slack (6%), as potential efficiency gains are outweighed by patient care risks. This study offers data-driven insights for healthcare decision-makers.

Title: A scheduling problem in a reconfigurable manufacturing system with stochastic worker availability: a hybrid L-shaped decomposition method
Authors: Hessam Bakhshi-Khaniki, Reza Tavakkoli-Moghaddam, Zdenek Hanzalek, Behdin Vahedi-Nouri
Affiliations: University of Tehran; Istinye University; Czech Institute of Informatics Robotics and Cybernetics, Czech Technical University in Prague
Abstract: Modern manufacturing faces growing challenges from market volatility, resource uncertainty, and the need for quick adaptation. Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems (RMSs) offer a flexible adaptable solution; however, scheduling becomes more complex when worker availability is uncertain. Workers in RMSs represent limited and mobile resources, whose uncertain availability can severely disrupt production efficiency. This paper investigates the non-identical parallel machine scheduling problem in an RMS under stochastic worker availability. To tackle this complex optimisation problem, a two-stage stochastic programming model is developed. In the first stage, job-to-machine assignments are determined as here-and-now decisions. The second stage involves optimising job sequencing, machine configurations, and worker assignments after the worker availability scenarios are revealed. To solve this problem, a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model and an L-shaped Decomposition (LD) method are developed to minimise the expected makespan. To enhance solution efficiency, a novel CP-LD is proposed, where the master problem uses MILP while subproblems employ Constraint Programming (CP). Computational results show that the proposed CP-LD method outperforms the MILP and LD methods in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency. The sensitivity analysis provides insights into the impact of various system parameters on the expected makespan performance, highlighting the critical importance of workforce management.

Title: A hybrid solution approach for the joint optimisation of skeleton cut line layout and cutting path planning
Authors: Yuanpeng Lai, Shaowen Yao, Meng Tian, Hao Zhang, Congyi Wang, Jiewu Leng, Qiang Liu
Affiliations: Guangdong University of Technology; CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding Company Limited
Abstract: In CNC cutting scenarios such as large-scale shipbuilding, net-like scrap skeletons formed by cutting often lead to difficulties in separating nested parts, and their dimensions frequently exceed the handling limits of automated equipment or scrap containers, thus necessitating further segmentation. Existing ‘skeleton cut line’ (SCL) processes heavily rely on manual experience, making it difficult to balance scrap disposal requirements and processing efficiency. To address this, we propose the Joint Optimisation Problem of Skeleton Cut Line Layout and Cutting Path Planning, aiming to synergistically determine the SCL layout, cutting sequence, and entry points to minimise total processing costs under process constraints. We construct a mixed-integer linear programming model that integrates the Extended Precedence-Constrained Generalised Travelling Salesman Problem with the Weighted Set Covering Problem, and propose a two-stage heuristic hybrid solution approach of ‘geometry generation–dynamic optimisation’. The first stage constructs a finite high-quality candidate SCL set via geometric rules; the second employs a hybrid heuristic integrating Adaptive Large Neighbourhood Search, Simulated Annealing, and Local Search for efficient joint dynamic optimisation. Experiments on standard benchmarks and real-world industrial instances verify the model accuracy and demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in solution quality, efficiency, and robustness, confirming its practical applicability.

Title: Profit-oriented dynamic scheduling for disassembly flexible job shops: dealing with structural uncertainty and operation skipping
Authors: Zengyu Kuang, Hui Xie, Yinghui Ren, Xiaojun Zhuo, Minghao Shi
Affiliations: Hunan University; Changsha Research Institute of Mining and Metallurgy Co Ltd
Abstract: Disassembly scheduling for End-of-Life (EOL) products, particularly EV batteries, exhibits dynamic structural uncertainty and physical degradation characteristics. However, existing scheduling models are predominantly static and fail to fully capture the distinctive stochastic features and operation skipping patterns of such disassembly systems. To address these gaps, we formulate the process as a Markov Decision Process and propose a Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (H-MADRL) framework. To enhance practical applicability, a Hierarchical State Embedding module acts as a digital perception layer to quantify physical risks. Meanwhile, a Physics-Informed Dual-Agent mechanism coordinates task-machine assignments, and a Constraint-Compliant Masking layer ensures strict adherence to Standard Operating Procedures. Averaged over multiple independent runs, the framework achieves a 45.6% increase in profit rate and a 16.9% reduction in makespan compared to standard reinforcement learning and heuristic baselines. Ultimately, this approach secures shop-floor adaptability and significantly advances managerial precision in balancing economic density with operational throughput under stochastic constraints.

Title: Integrated production and truck–drone collaborative delivery scheduling problem to minimise the makespan
Authors: Lin Yuan, Zhaohong Jia, Yumei Huo
Affiliations: Anhui University; City University of New York
Abstract: This paper focuses on an integrated production and truck–drone collaborative delivery problem. The objective is to minimise the makespan. Jobs are first processed on a single machine in the factory and then distributed to their respective customers through a truck–drone pair in a back-and-forth manner. Specifically, the truck transports the processed jobs to the customer area, and at the parking point, the drone with limited flight endurance is launched to complete the final delivery to specific customer locations. Given that drone flight times vary across jobs, the general problem is shown to be strongly NP-hard. We identify two special cases that can be solved in polynomial time: (i) all jobs share the same drone flight time, and (ii) the number of distinct drone flight times is fixed. For both cases, we develop optimal algorithms. For the general case, we propose an approximation algorithm that integrates the First Fit Decreasing algorithm with Johnson's rule. Comprehensive numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Title: Vehicle routing for on-site services with time window flexibility and time-dependent speeds to minimise emission cost
Authors: Yizi Zhou, Jiyin Liu, Rupal Mandania
Affiliations: Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.; People’s Republic of China; Loughborough University
Abstract: We study the problem of scheduling engineers who drive to customer sites to perform service tasks. Vehicle speeds and associated CO2 emissions are time-dependent. Customers specify a service time window or choose to participate in a green delivery programme by offering multiple available time windows. This new vehicle routing problem with multiple time windows and time-dependent speeds is formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model to minimise emission costs. The model is then extended to handle scenarios in which customers can offer optional time windows on different days. To solve large instances, we develop a self-adaptive simulated annealing algorithm. For small instances solvable by optimisation software, experimental results show that the algorithm produces near-optimal solutions efficiently. Experiments on instances of different sizes show consistent improvement of the proposed algorithm over the standard simulated annealing. The algorithm is further applied in additional experiments simulating more practical operations. Results demonstrate that incorporating time window flexibility can reduce emission costs and increase the number of customers served under overbooking conditions. Tests under various settings indicate that greater participation in the green delivery programme, or more available time windows per customer, leads to further reductions in emission costs and improved service capacity.

Title: More information, better forecasting? Empirical evidence from integrating customer sentiment and Google Trends
Authors: Ristanti Ramadanti, Vasileios Bougioukos, Konstantinos Nikolopoulos
Affiliations: University of Manchester; Richmond American University of London; Durham University Business School
Abstract: Our study delves into a major – and yet a largely unanswered research question in the forecasting literature: does the integration of additional information into forecasting models improve forecasting performance? We experiment with incorporating customer sentiment and/or auxiliary data (Google Trends) into both statistical and advanced machine-learning forecasting models; the latter is used to examine whether this additional information is better utilised linearly or non-linearly. This is a methodological contribution that focuses on the added value of additional information; it is not a paper on the performance of specific models or methods, which are used in this research only as representatives of their class, predominantly to capture nonlinearities. The empirical setting involves forecasting sales of gaming consoles from Nintendo, Sony PlayStation, and Microsoft Xbox, using customer reviews on Amazon and Google Trends search trend data. We compared the sentiment-extraction tools VADER and TextBlob, and our results favoured the former; thus, the choice of tool matters. The most important finding was that forecasting sales using Google Trends and customer-review-related variables generally increases prediction accuracy, and there is preliminary evidence that this additional information is better utilised by non-linear models (i.e., Random Forests).

Title: Methodology to design a technology-enabled circular manufacturing system
Authors: Maxence Denu, Pierre David, Fabien Mangione, Aurélie Landry
Affiliations: Grenoble Institute of Engineering, University of Grenoble Alpes

Title: The multi-AMR buffer storage, retrieval, and reshuffling problem: a mathematical model and hierarchical heuristic
Authors: Max Disselnmeyer, Thomas Bömer, Laura Dörr, Bastian Amberg, Anne Meyer
Affiliations: Institute for Information Management in Engineering (IMI), Karlsruhe Institute of Technology
Abstract: Buffer zones are essential in production systems to decouple sequential processes. In dense floor storage environments, such as space-constrained brownfield facilities, manual operation is increasingly challenged by severe labor shortages and rising operational costs. Automating these zones requires solving the Buffer Storage, Retrieval, and Reshuffling Problem (BSRRP). While previous work has addressed scenarios where the focus is limited to reshuffling and retrieving a fixed set of items, real-world manufacturing necessitates an adaptive approach that also incorporates arriving unit loads. This paper introduces the Multi-AMR BSRRP, coordinating a robot fleet to manage concurrent reshuffling, alongside time-windowed storage and retrieval tasks, within a shared floor area. We formulate a Binary Integer Programming (IP) model to obtain exact solutions for benchmarking purposes. As the problem is NP-hard, rendering exact methods computationally intractable for industrial scales, we propose a hierarchical heuristic. This approach decomposes the problem into an A* search for task-level sequence planning of unit load placements, and a Constraint Programming (CP) approach for multi-robot coordination and scheduling. Experiments demonstrate orders-of-magnitude computation time reductions compared to the exact formulation. These results confirm the heuristic's viability as responsive control logic for high-density production environments.

Title: Strategic lean practices for Industry 5.0 manufacturing
Authors: Peder Veng Søberg, Rasmus Sorth, Samuel Brüning Larsen
Affiliations: Technical University of Denmark, DTU Engineering Technology, Ballerup, Denmark; Pharmaceutical and Medical Devices Industries, Copenhagen, Denmark
Abstract: This study examines how strategic lean practices (SLPs), including Hoshin Kanri, catchball processes, lean improvement tools, and digital diagnostic capabilities, support the transition toward human-centered, resilient Industry 5.0 manufacturing systems. Drawing on knowledge management theory, strategy deployment literature, and research on Industry 4.0 and 5.0, the study conducts a comparative analysis of four manufacturing cases. The findings suggest that stronger diagnostic infrastructures, including value stream mapping (VSM), dashboards, heat maps, and other digital performance visibility tools, support richer knowledge management processes by enabling more robust combination and internalisation processes within the SECI model. The cases further demonstrate that digitalisation reduces the manual burden associated with data collection and problem identification, enabling organisations to focus more on longitudinal analysis, prioritisation, and continuous improvement. The study also highlights how overly granular target structures can lead to dysfunctional local optimisation, whereas more aggregated strategic deployment mechanisms can strengthen shared ownership across organisational functions. The paper contributes a contingent decision framework for selecting strategic lean practices depending on the strategic challenge, available diagnostic capabilities, and desired Industry 5.0 outcomes.

Title: Country level blockchain readiness index for firms in supply chains: an empirical study
Authors: Jennifer Lazzeri Gracia-Campo, Laurence Saglietto, Yuan Yao, Delphine David, Rami Alkhudary, Pierre Féniès
Affiliations: Aix-Marseille Université, CRET-LOG; Université Côte D’Azur IAE Nice, GREDEG CNRS; Université Sorbonne Paris Nord; Université Paris-Panthéon-Assas, LARGEPA
Abstract: This study addresses a gap in the literature by proposing and empirically validating a novel, integrated decision tool for blockchain adoption in supply chains, the Country Level Blockchain Readiness Index for Firms in Supply Chains (CLBRI-FSC). The index integrates five dimensions, including financial support, information technology infrastructure, logistics infrastructure, human capital, and organisational capital. Based on established theoretical frameworks, the index uses secondary data from the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). It employs Min–Max normalisation to standardise indicators and cosine similarity. It calculates readiness scores, offering a replicable and data-driven metric. Results highlight regional differences. Organisations in Northern and Western European countries like Finland, Denmark, Norway, and Belgium show strong readiness in financial and technological infrastructure. Organisations in Southern European countries such as Italy and Portugal exhibit greater readiness in human and organisational capital, reflecting more managerial flexibility and skill development. Organisations in Central and Eastern European countries, including Romania and Bulgaria, show low readiness across most dimensions due to financial, infrastructural, and institutional challenges. The findings provide insights for managers, industry, and policymakers to develop supportive strategies for blockchain adoption.

Title: A degradation modelling framework integrating prediction uncertainty and imperfect maintenance for maintenance strategy optimisation
Authors: Cheng Wang, Mengna Hu, Pai Zheng, Lili Deng
Affiliations: Zhejiang University of Technology; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
Abstract: In modern industry, proactive maintenance is crucial for preventing failures and reducing costs. However, most existing data-driven prognostic frameworks remain limited in their ability to support realistic maintenance decisions, primarily due to a persistent disconnect between predictive modelling and maintenance modelling. While deep learning methods have advanced life prediction accuracy, they often neglect the pervasive reality of imperfect maintenance (IM), where maintenance actions only partially restore equipment health. This disconnect is compounded when IM modelling, traditionally grounded in reliability statistics, is not adapted to leverage real-time, data-driven predictions and their associated uncertainties. To bridge this gap, this study proposes an innovative integrated framework that closes the loop between uncertainty-aware prediction and maintenance optimisation. Our core contribution is a systematic methodology that includes: a novel Weighted Interval Fusion (WIF) method for high-confidence remaining useful life (RUL) prediction; a hybrid degradation model that uses Bayesian inference to dynamically select the most suitable IM model; and a dynamic maintenance strategy guided by a risk perception function, which explicitly couples prediction uncertainty with failure urgency. Extensive experiments show that our framework not only improves prediction accuracy but also yields more cost-effective and reliable maintenance strategies, thereby providing a prescriptive foundation for intelligent maintenance.

Title: A decomposition-based approach for assembly line balancing problems
Authors: Jordi Pereira, Mariona Vilà
Affiliations: UPF – Barcelona School of Management; EAE Business School
Abstract: Assembly lines are widely used for mass production. Their design and operation of such systems involve the resolution of multiple problems, among which the assembly line balancing problem (ALBP) is one of the most studied. An ALBP typically involves at least two interrelated decisions aimed at optimising line efficiency: (1) determining the sequence in which operations must be performed within the assembly line and (2) assigning these tasks to the stations that constitute the assembly line. This study presents a general methodology for solving a broad range of ALBPs based on the observation that many such problems can be decomposed into interrelated subproblems. The proposed method leverages the fact that once a task sequence is fixed, optimal station assignments can be obtained through a dynamic programming (DP) recursion. To illustrate the proposed methodology, we derive DP formulations for multiple ALBP variants and integrate them into heuristic frameworks that explore a solution space represented by task sequences. Computational experiments using a genetic algorithm and a local search procedure demonstrate the adaptability and effectiveness of the proposed approach. In particular, for sequence-dependent and chance-constrained assembly line balancing problems, the method achieves higher-quality solutions in shorter computational times than current state-of-the-art techniques.

Title: From Huygens to Industry 4.0: a review of synchronisation mechanisms and performance impacts
Authors: Sanghita Bose, Julia Arlinghaus, Marc-Thorsten Hütt
Affiliations: Constructor University Bremen; University of St. Gallen
Abstract: Synchronisation as a logistics concept aims to harmonise material and information flows in production systems and supply chains across different organisations. For instance, in the automotive industry, the Just-in-Sequence concept synchronises suppliers' parts production with manufacturers' assembly, thereby reducing lead times, improving due date reliability, and lowering inventories along the supply chain. Synchronisation has emerged as a key approach to balance logistics performance, cost efficiency, and resilience demands in complex global production networks. In parallel, synchronisation as a physics concept has gained relevance, with applications in architecture, biology, and mechanics. This review article seeks to consolidate these diverse perspectives by examining how synchronisation is conceptualised in logistics and physics. Our aim is to identify potential pathways through which synchronisation mediates both negative and positive effects, thereby contributing to the performance of global production and supply chains. We use a discrete event simulation of a simplified Just-in-Sequence system to illustrate key impact factors of the two synchronisation types. Based on this foundation, we analyze 81 publications from 1986 to 2025 and identify the mathematical foundations of different synchronisation measures and conceptualizations, and describe their linkages to key performance indicators used in industrial practice. The findings provide insights for both scholars and practitioners seeking to better understand the dynamics of complex value systems and to leverage synchronisation as a means of enhancing operational performance.

Title: Robust CP and PPO-driven matheuristic methods for multi-ship co-dock maintenance scheduling considering uncertainty and limited dock capacity
Authors: Zheng Gao, Chao Dai, Liping Zhang, Zikai Zhang, Zixiang Li, Yu Zhang
Affiliations: Key Laboratory of Metallurgical Equipment and Control Technology, Ministry of Education, Wuhan University of Science and Technology, Wuhan; Wuhan University of Science and Technology; Beihang University; China Institute of Marine Technology & Economy
Abstract: Unreasonable allocation of dock resources can easily cause maintenance task blockage during ship maintenance operations. Moreover, uncertain ship arrival time due to external factors poses significant challenges for maintenance scheduling. Therefore, this work investigates a multi-ship co-dock maintenance scheduling problem with limited dock capacity and uncertain ship arrival time. To solve this problem efficiently, this work first employs chance-constrained programming to address uncertain ship arrival time. It is then integrated with a constraint programming (CP) model to generate a robust multi-ship co-dock maintenance schedule. Meanwhile, a PPO-driven matheuristic algorithm is further developed to improve the solution efficiency for larger instances. The PPO-driven matheuristic integrates proximal policy optimisation (PPO) and the CP decomposition model. PPO adaptively adjusts the search behaviour. Meanwhile, the CP decomposition model performs local refinements to further improve promising solutions. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed CP model and the PPO-driven matheuristic. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the CP model. Compared with the mixed-integer programming model, it delivers significantly better solving performance. The key components of the PPO-driven matheuristic algorithm contribute positively to algorithmic performance, and the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art metaheuristic algorithms.

Title: An investigation into human related factors for enhanced supply chain resilience: a systematic literature review
Authors: Yueheng Zhang, Laura Purvis, Yuan Huang, Yingli Wang
Affiliations: Cardiff University; University of York
Abstract: In today's turbulent business environment, the significance of supply chain resilience (SCRES) has surged. Although SCRES capabilities and their potential impact on performance have been extensively explored, supply chain management (SCM) remains human-centric and depends heavily on individuals and teams making effective decisions. However, the extant literature on individual- and team-level capabilities required to enhance SCRES remains fragmented. This study addresses this gap through a systematic literature review (SLR) of extant knowledge in this area. We develop an integrative framework of Dynamic Human-related Capabilities for resilience by extending the Dynamic Managerial Capability (DMC) theory to examine how individuals and teams enhance SCRES. Although relevant, DMC theory mainly emphasises managers’ roles within organisations. To provide a more comprehensive understanding of human related capabilities for enhanced SCRES, we extend the analysis to employees and teams, within and across organisations. We examine research inquiries and analytical models from 77 studies, focusing on three dynamic human-related capabilities: (i) social capital, (ii) human capital, and (iii) cognition. We identify key practices associated with each capability and explain their roles in enhancing SCRES. Furthermore, we propose a future research agenda that puts human-centric factors at the core of SCRES.

Title: Which type of influencer should the brand cooperate with in the livestream e-commerce supply chain: coupon-driven or content-oriented?
Authors: Tong-Yuan Wang, Bin Li, Victor Shi
Affiliations: Henan University; Wilfrid Laurier University
Abstract: The increasing sophistication of livestream selling (LSS) makes it crucial for brands to select the optimal cooperation strategy. Concurrently, influencers employ two distinct LSS strategies: one driven by coupons, and the other content-oriented. Against this backdrop, we build four game-theoretic models to identify the optimal strategy for different brands (i.e. start-up brands and established brands) to cooperate with two types of influencers (i.e. coupon-driven influencers and content-oriented influencers). Our results indicate that a start-up brand’s optimal cooperation strategy shifts from the content-oriented influencer to the coupon-driven influencer as the commission rate, brand-value enhancement coefficient, and influencer fan base increase. By contrast, established brands should prioritise content-oriented influencers to leverage content advantages for enhancing brand value, potentially creating a win-win-win outcome for the brand, the influencer, and consumers under high-quality content creation and effective audience engagement. Moreover, increasing brand awareness may reduce the incentive for established brands to cooperate with content-oriented influencers. Surprisingly, the coupon-driven influencer may be less effective than the content-oriented influencer in boosting product sales. Overall, this paper integrates LSS into operations and supply chain management practices, offering valuable managerial insights for firms’ digital transformation.

Title: Enhancing lasso tactical demand forecasts using semantic information
Authors: Yves R. Sagaert, Nikolaos Kourentzes
Affiliations: VIVES University of Applied Sciences; University of Skövde, Stockholm, Sweden
Abstract: Leading indicators have been shown to be useful in predicting demand. Nowadays, a large number of potentially interesting variables are available in open databases. This makes it challenging to select the predictively relevant indicators. Lasso regression has become a popular choice when handling many variables, however, its selection is sensitive to changes in the sample and in the presence of correlated variables. This can harm both its predictive performance and the trustworthiness of the forecasts. We consider various approaches to aid variable selection. Specifically, we consider clustering via various statistical based methods, semantic information using a Semantic Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, or meta-data, such as a popularity index of variables. The resulting groups of variables are evaluated for selection directly, using sequential lasso, or transformed into cluster profiles, or factors using principal component analysis. Using an empirical case, we evaluate the alternative options on their decision and predictive performance, and on the interpretability of the resulting models. Our analysis indicates that there are trade-offs between predictive and decision performance, and interpretability. Semantic information is found to benefit variable selection, although we do not identify a dominant approach. Finally, we emphasise the need for methodological advances for explainability in forecasting.HighlightsWe compare different groupings of variables to enhance selection with lasso.Groupings are based on statistical, semantic, and meta-data information.Additional dimensionality reduction by cluster profiles and factors is investigated.Semantic information leads to gains in forecast and decision metrics.Credibly explainable models should match or outperform non-explainable benchmarks.

Title: Digital twin-driven human-machine collaborative maintenance services for continuous slab caster
Authors: Baotong Chen, Yu (Eve) Zhang, Jiafu Wan, Lei Wang, Miguel Martínez-García, Xuhui Xia, Jiangting Zhu, Lisa Jackson
Affiliations: (Wuhan University of Science and Technology), Ministry of Education, Wuhan University of Science and Technology; Wuhan University of Science and Technology; Loughborough University; South China University of Technology; Guangzhou Railway Polytechnic
Abstract: Continuous slab caster is an important piece of metallurgical equipment in the iron and steel industry. The present maintenance service for complex metallurgical equipment is often inseparable from the experience knowledge of the maintenance professionals. Digital twin (DT) offers new approaches to intelligent maintenance for slab casters, as they are able to reflect the operational process of the physical equipment in a virtual space, including the cyber model, operation history, and real time sensor update. This paper mainly explores DT-driven human-machine collaborative maintenance services for the continuous slab caster. Firstly, DT model is constructed by digitally correlating the equipment operation process, enabling performance evaluation and failure prediction. Then, by integrating human expert knowledge, a multi-layer knowledge base of the domain maintenance is created to facilitate the service recommendation based on digital maps. This forms an intelligent maintenance mechanism bridging human and machine collaboration. Finally, the effect of the DT-driven maintenance scheme on slab caster engineering was verified by its application to a steel plant. Preliminary statistical results shown that this approach reduced maintenance costs and improved maintenance efficiency under the harsh metallurgical environments, and maintenance intelligence was improved through the DT-driven human-machine collaboration scheme.

Title: A knowledge-lite reinforcement learning framework for online scheduling in human–robot collaborative customized production systems
Authors: Hao Tang, Zifeng Wang, Nan Zhou, Yonghui Zhang, Bo Xu, Uzair Aslam Bhatti
Affiliations: Hainan University; Pengcheng Laboratory
Abstract: To accommodate the increasing demand for personalized customization, manufacturing enterprises must enhance the flexibility of their production lines while efficiently allocating limited robotic resources under strict time constraints. This study tackles the multi-objective scheduling challenges inherent in dynamic, human–robot collaborative (HRC), and highly customized production environments by introducing a knowledge-lite reinforcement learning (KLRL) framework. Unlike traditional rule-based approaches, the KLRL framework employs a hierarchical multi-network architecture in which job and robot features are encoded as state matrices, and scheduling actions are directly derived from the mapping relationships among production factors – thus eliminating the dependence on predefined dispatching rules. The method explicitly incorporates dynamic factors, including stochastic job arrivals and cancelations, scheduled maintenance, robot breakdowns, and human reconfiguration of robots to adapt to new manufacturing processes. Multiple objectives, including makespan, job tardiness, robot utilization, and number of human–robot interactions, are jointly optimized through a dynamic learning mechanism. Extensive experiments across various production scales demonstrate that KLRL delivers superior or comparable performance to composite dispatching rules and state-of-the-art reinforcement learning (RL) methods, thereby validating its effectiveness in complex, human–robot collaborative, and customized scheduling scenarios.

Title: Reviewing lean manufacturing and Industry 4.0 technologies in the supply chain
Authors: John Reyes, Josefa Mula, Manuel Diaz-Madroñero
Affiliations: Universidad Técnica de Ambato; Universitat Politècnica de València
Abstract: This paper aims to provide a literature review of how lean manufacturing (LM) and Industry 4.0 (I4.0) technologies are integrated in a supply chain (SC) context. The PRISMA methodology is followed for data collection in the Web of Science and Scopus databases, where 92 papers were selected and reviewed. The analytic categories were based on the following: (1) SC structure; (2) decision levels; (3) research methodology and modelling approach; (4) lean waste types; (5) development tools, LM tools and I4.0 technologies; (6) practical application; (7) benefits and SC performance; (8) limitations. The main results provide a compilation of the literature on real-world waste and I4.0 planning challenges that are specific to certain sectors. The research focused mainly on conceptual, descriptive and exploratory methodologies. The case study was the main empirical modelling approach, followed by mathematical programming and simulation models. The lean tools that are most integrated with I4.0 technologies are kanban, just in time (JIT) and total productive maintenance. The Internet of Things (IoT), big data and cloud computing stand out for having more interactions with LM tools.

Title: Live-streaming selling considering consumer returns: manufacturer’s choice of streamer types and return freight insurance policies
Authors: Ping He, Shunan Guo, Xinru Chen, Xiangling Hu
Affiliations: South China University of Technology; Anhui University; Grand Valley State University
Abstract: The prevalence of live-streaming selling greatly impacts consumer returns, which forms an urgent challenge for manufacturers to implement return freight insurance (RFI) policies and live-streaming operations appropriately. In the paper, we establish a supply chain where a manufacturer deploys an employee or influencer streamer to sell products on a live-streaming platform and introduces three kinds of RFI policies, namely no-RFI (NRFI) policy, manufacturers-RFI (MRFI) policy, and consumers-RFI (CRFI) policy. Given that the interaction-perception efficiency of streamers may positively or negatively affect the return rate, we explore the choice of streamer types and RFI policies, yielding several significant findings. First, with the MRFI policy, the manufacturer should deploy an influencer streamer at a low MRFI fee and high residual value; otherwise, it should deploy an employee streamer. Second, with the CRFI policy, the manufacturer should deploy an influencer streamer at a high CRFI fee or high product residual value; otherwise, it should deploy an employee streamer. Finally, regardless of which streamer is deployed, the manufacturer consistently adopts the MRFI policy at a low MRFI fee. However, when the MRFI fee exceeds a certain threshold, the CRFI fee and the interaction-perception efficiency affect the choice between CRFI and NRFI policies.

Title: Blockchain-enabled transparency in low-carbon supply chains: a dynamic Stackelberg differential game approach
Authors: Imad El Harraki, Karim Zkik, Amine Belhadi, Sunil Tiwari, Sachin Kamble
Affiliations: Ecole Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Rabat; Rennes School of Business; Rabat Business School, Rabat Business School; University of Bristol Business School; EDHEC Business School
Abstract: This paper develops a dynamic Stackelberg differential game model, inspired by the classical Sethi advertising model, to address coordination and transparency challenges in low-carbon supply chains (LCSC). Recognising the strategic importance of blockchain-enabled transparency, we integrate blockchain investment decisions into a stochastic differential game model to examine how transparency reduces information asymmetry and greenwashing while enhancing sustainable competitiveness. We formulate a hierarchical supply chain comprising a low-carbon firm (LCF) as the leader and a high-carbon firm (HCF) as the follower, with pricing, advertising, and blockchain investment decisions evolving under uncertainty. The model extends Sethi's seminal contributions by incorporating blockchain-enabled transparency as a dynamic state variable that influences both demand and equilibrium coordination. The equilibrium results show that blockchain-enabled transparency increases the LCF's long-term market share by approximately 15–20%, improves profitability by up to 25%, and reduces advertising costs by 30% compared to non-blockchain scenarios. Numerical simulations confirm that the benefits of blockchain are most pronounced when transparency and communication are jointly optimised. The findings provide theoretical and managerial insights into how blockchain-enabled transparency can help firms achieve both competitiveness and sustainability in low-carbon supply chains.

Title: Leveraging large language models to enhance multi-agent risk assessment in supply chain networks
Authors: Yinzhu Quan, Zefang Liu, Frederick Benaben, Benoit Montreuil
Affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology; IMT Mines Albi
Abstract: We propose a novel large language model (LLM) enhanced framework, MARS (Multi-Agent Risk assessment in Supply chain networks), for risk assessment and integration of both structured and unstructured factors for logistic hub site selection across a target territory, using the southeastern U.S. states as a testbed. While structured factors such as cost, distance, traffic accidents, traffic congestion, and crime rates can be directly computed, unstructured severe weather event narratives need to be interpreted semantically through LLMs. We introduce a multi-agent architecture featuring three specialised agents, RiskAgent, FeedbackAgent, and RevisionAgent, that collaborate through a feedback-revision loop to convert raw extreme weather event narratives into fine-grained risk severity levels. By integrating these severity levels with structured indicators via aggregation, the proposed method enables interpretable and risk-aware ranking of candidate hubs, thereby supporting informed decision-making for logistic hub site selection.

Title: Automatic demand forecast model selection in supply chains: a forecast value-added analysis of selection strategies, machine learning, and hyperparameter optimisation
Authors: Wassim Garred, Raphaël Oger, Matthieu Lauras
Affiliations: Université de Toulouse; Kedge Business School
Abstract: Demand forecasting plays a critical role in supply chain management, enabling suppliers, manufacturers, and retailers to synchronise operations and enhance overall efficiency. Despite extensive research on time series forecast model selection, choosing the most appropriate forecasting model for a given time series remains a complex challenge, particularly in volatile and uncertain environments. The increasing availability of data and the emergence of new forecasting methods have introduced greater complexity, making automated model selection essential for improving forecasting accuracy and decision-making in supply chain operations. This study proposes an automated demand forecast model selection framework that integrates a broad range of statistical and machine learning models. A key feature of the framework is the optimisation of hyperparameters across all models, ensuring each method is fine-tuned for optimal performance. The approach is validated on the M3 monthly dataset, where it outperforms all previously submitted methods, demonstrating significant improvements in forecast accuracy. Additionally, the methodology is tested in a real-world supply chain setting, further showcasing its effectiveness in handling complex and dynamic demand patterns. By enhancing forecast accuracy and reducing the reliance on manual model selection, this research provides an efficient decision support system for supply chain demand forecasting in fast-changing supply chain environments.

Title: Diffusion model-based generative optimisation for resilient service composition in cloud manufacturing
Authors: Erfan Shahab, Pourya Moghadam, Sharareh Taghipour
Affiliations: Toronto Metropolitan University; University of Toronto
Abstract: Recent disruptions in supply networks highlight the need for resilient, data-driven decision support. We propose a novel multi-stage optimisation framework that integrates deep generative models with operations planning to address dynamic resource allocation under disruptions. Specifically, a variational autoencoder (VAE) learns a latent manifold of feasible allocation plans, and a diffusion-based generative model produces realistic refined disruption-aware allocations. These components combine in a stage-wise optimisation process. The approach yields flexible allocation strategies that adapt in real time to evolving uncertainties, improving overall network resilience. We demonstrate practical relevance of our method through a case study with disruptions, where our generative-optimisation framework outperforms traditional optimisation by providing faster adaptation and better performance under disturbance. This work highlights the novelty of embedding generative AI into production decision support. By leveraging learned latent spaces and diffusion processes, it offers a new direction for operations research tools that blend generative modelling with optimisation, enhancing resilient and informed decision-making. The computational approach scales to realistic planning problems and provides decision-makers with actionable insights. Overall, our results suggest that generative optimisation can serve as a practical decision-support tool for managing network disruptions.

Title: Live-streaming E-commerce operations: is it wise for manufacturers to use AI streamers when human streamers face a goodwill crisis?
Authors: Xiaojun Fan, Lu Zhang
Affiliations: Shanghai University
Abstract: In addition to selling products directly to consumers in traditional online channels through an e-platform at a traditional online price, a manufacturer sells products in live-streaming channels by employing a human streamer. Human streamers with goodwill can attract additional consumers (fan size). However, they may make erroneous statements during live-streaming sales, triggering a goodwill crisis that damages product sales. In response, some manufacturers invest in artificial intelligence (AI) streamers to support product sales in traditional online channels, but at investment costs. However, most existing literature focuses on the human streamer’s fan size and rarely considers goodwill crises. Therefore, we develop a game-theoretic model to examine the impact of goodwill crises and further explore manufacturers’ preferences for human and AI streamers. The main findings are as follows. Intuitively, when the crisis damage degree is high, manufacturers invest in AI streamers. However, we find that only when the human streamer’s fan size is low, manufacturers choose AI streamers that are profitable if the crisis damage degree is high. Otherwise, manufacturers still choose human streamers. Further, manufacturers investing in AI streamers can increase the e-platform’s profit.

Title: Mining novel customer needs for product design from user-generated content through large language model-enabled data augmentation and ensemble learning
Authors: Shaoqin Huang, Hu Qin, Yue Wang
Affiliations: The Education University of Hong Kong; Huazhong University of Science and Technology
Abstract: Detecting novel customer needs from user-generated content such as online product reviews is essential for supporting product innovation and improving customer satisfaction. However, challenges arise due to severe class imbalance, where only a small portion of the content reflects truly novel needs, and the presence of noisy or irrelevant information. In response, this paper presents a new framework that combines generative artificial intelligence with ensemble learning. We use LLaMA, a powerful open-source large language model, to generate diverse meaningful positive samples that reduce data sparsity. With this augmented dataset, we train multiple BERT-based classifiers, each on different subsets of the data, and integrate their predictions using a hard voting strategy to improve accuracy and robustness. Experiments on a dataset of Amazon laptop reviews show that the proposed method achieves superior performance in recall and F1 score compared with standard baselines. This performance capability helps ensure that valuable insights are not missed. We offer a practical approach for applying generative models to support product development, laying the foundation for future studies in artificial intelligence for business innovation.

Title: Optimal pricing and livestreaming selling decisions under duopoly competition: an influencer marketing perspective
Authors: Lei Xiao, Zhiwen Li, Qingguo Bai, Xiaohua Han
Affiliations: Hubei University; Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics; Qufu Normal University; Guangdong University of Foreign Studies
Abstract: Considering market competition, this paper explores the optimal pricing and livestreaming selling decisions of two competing brands from the perspective of influencer marketing. Given the role of social influencers in activating high-value consumers (or their followers), we develop a modified vertical differentiation model to explore the optimal pricing and livestreaming selling decisions of duopolistic brands. Then, we analyze the impacts of the optimal decisions on consumer surplus and social welfare. Lastly, we relax relevant assumptions to explore more generalised scenarios. We find that when both brands use the same livestreaming selling strategies, the low-quality brand's cost-free quality improvement may harm both the competitor and itself, but with livestreaming introduced, it may stop harming the competitor and boost its own performance. The stronger marketing capabilities of social influencers directly benefit partner brands and conditionally help competitors. As social influencers' marketing capabilities improve, both brands will successively encounter three different livestreaming sales scenarios. That is, from the scenario where no brand adopts the livestreaming sales mode, to the scenario where only a single brand adopts this mode, and finally to the scenario where both brands adopt this mode. Livestreaming selling erodes base consumers' welfare by raising prices and reducing demand, but it boosts consumer surplus by attracting high-valuation additional consumers and enhances overall social welfare by softening competition and expanding demand.

Title: Intelligent scheduling in agricultural wholesale markets: an optimisation approach with simulation-driven and GenAI-based interaction support
Authors: Kotomichi Matsuno, Hiroki Iizuka, Che-Wei Chou, Takahiro Ohno
Affiliations: Rissho University, Tokyo; Waseda University, Tokyo; Feng chia University, Taichung
Abstract: This study addresses truck congestion at Japanese agricultural wholesale markets by proposing a novel simulation-driven scheduling system that integrates optimisation and Generative AI (GenAI)-based interaction interface. Congestion caused by upstream scheduling constraints and limited unloading space results in excessive waiting, increased CO2 emissions, and deteriorating labour conditions. In the proposed system, a genetic algorithm under fairness constraints is used to minimise total operational and waiting times by utilising real-time data on truck size, shipment content, unloading duration, and spatial constraints. Additionally, a GenAI-based interaction system provides dynamic instructions to drivers, enhancing their compliance. Simulation experiments using data reflecting actual market conditions demonstrated that, compared to the conventional first-come-first-served method, the proposed system can reduce total unloading time by nearly 10% and average waiting time by over 20%. Furthermore, by reducing truck idling during peak hours, the system contributes to measurable reductions in truck idling–related CO2 emissions, reinforcing its practical relevance for sustainable logistics operations. Overall, the proposed system enhances logistics efficiency and labour conditions, providing an empirical digital transformation paradigm for agricultural wholesale markets.

Title: Reshaping coopetition: strategic sharing of the semiconductor manufacturing supply chain risk management capabilities
Authors: Jun Pei, Hongqing Kuang, Wenjuan Fan, Panos M. Pardalos
Affiliations: Hefei University of Technology; University of Florida
Abstract: As global supply chains become increasingly complex, it is vital to enhance the resilience of semiconductor manufacturing supply chains for sustainable development. We focus on the strategic choice of the semiconductor manufacturer to improve resilience by opening the supply chain risk management (SCRM) platform and sharing its capabilities. In practice, semiconductor manufacturers typically procure semi-finished products from semiconductor suppliers, who also compete with manufacturers in the downstream market. This coopetitive relationship introduces additional complexity into the manufacturer's sharing decision. To analyze this dynamic, we develop a game-theoretic model to analyze the optimal sharing decision. First, our study finds that even when the revenue from the supplier's access is lower than the costs incurred from access, the semiconductor manufacturer sometimes still opens the platform. Then, the semiconductor manufacturer may invest more in the platform even when the product value is relatively low. Additionally, while accessing the platform improves the supplier's technical performance, capability sharing constitutes a win–win strategy only under certain conditions. Furthermore, capability sharing may lead to improvements in both customer surplus and social welfare. Our findings provide valuable insights for semiconductor manufacturers' decisions on SCRM capability sharing, suppliers' response mechanisms, and relevant policy formulation.

Title: Energy-aware and ergonomic storage assignment in human-robot collaborative order picking systems
Authors: Xiaowei Li, Guowei Hua, T. C. E. Cheng
Affiliations: China University of Geosciences (Beijing); Beijing Jiaotong University; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
Abstract: The growing adoption of automation in warehousing has underscored the importance of ergonomics and human factors in order picking. Traditional storage assignment strategies often prioritise throughput and travel distance while overlooking the physical and cognitive workload on human pickers. This study introduces an energy-aware ergonomic storage assignment framework that integrates biomechanical energy expenditure modelling, safety constraints, and heuristic optimisation. It begins with constructing an energy expenditure cost matrix that incorporates workload parameters, capturing both physical lifting and cognitive search demands. Ergonomic constraints are then formulated to regulate total rack load, ensuring occupational safety. An exact optimisation formulation is first introduced to characterise optimal ergonomic storage assignments, complemented by a greedy-based heuristic procedure to support computationally efficient solution generation. Numerical studies reveal that this method achieves significant energy expenditure savings by approximately 47% compared with baseline strategies while strictly adhering to hard safety constraints. Sensitivity analyses illustrate how key performance measures vary with problem scale, providing insights into the model’s behaviour under different parameter settings. The findings enhance research on human-centric warehouse optimisation and provide actionable guidelines for developing ergonomic, safe, and efficient storage assignment policies in intralogistics systems.

Title: Managing the two-tier healthcare system: referral discounts and artificial intelligence-based diagnosis
Authors: Xiaofang Wang, Chenhe Pan, Yixuan Liu, Guoming Lai
Affiliations: Renmin University of China; China Europe International Business School (CEIBS); The University of Texas at Austin
Abstract: Without professional assistance, patients cannot accurately identify their severity and thus often make inappropriate choice among tiered care providers. Recently, artificial intelligence- based diagnosis (AI-based diagnosis) is widely used to help patients make better treatment choice in addition to traditional financial incentives. In this paper, we develop a strategic queueing model, where a low-level provider (GP) may refer patients to a high-level provider (SP) and the patients can strategically choose where to go for initial treatment after seeking AI advice. We find that the common practice of discounting the SP's treatment fees for referred patients may not be able to close the social welfare gap between market equilibrium and social optimum while this gap can always be closed by adjusting the SP's treatment fees together with such referral discounts. Moreover, social welfare can be improved by increasing the AI diagnostic accuracy. This effect becomes more significant when the GP has a higher error probability of treating a truly severe patient but may be less significant when the GP is more likely to refer a truly non-severe patient, depending on the SP's capacity. Finally, the two-tier healthcare system may be worse off using AI-based diagnosis under some circumstances.

Title: Decision support for the integrated flexible job shop scheduling and operator timetabling problem
Authors: Reza Ghorbani Saber, Pieter Leyman, El-Houssaine Aghezzaf
Affiliations: Ghent University; Flanders Make@UGent
Abstract: This paper addresses the integrated Flexible Job Shop Scheduling and Operator Timetabling (FJS-OT) problem, which incorporates shift-based constraints reflecting operators' timetabling regulations. To support practitioners in making informed decisions, we first enhance the existing mixed-integer programming (MIP) formulation to improve its scalability for industrial-sized instances. We then introduce two new solution approaches: a Logic-Based Benders Decomposition (LBBD) and a matheuristic algorithm, both tailored for medium to large problem sizes. In addition, we develop a tabu search metaheuristic to the FJS-OT problem, building on a version known for its effectiveness in handling industrial-scale flexible job shop instances. This collection of approaches offers scalable decision support, depending on the problem size, available computational resources, and optimality requirements. Computational experiments demonstrate that LBBD outperforms the MIP model on small- to medium-sized instances, while the matheuristic efficiently delivers high-quality solutions for larger cases. For very large instances, the tabu search method proves capable of rapidly generating feasible solutions where other methods may fall short. This tool is currently undergoing testing in industrial environments, providing practical guidance for production planners facing challenging FJS-OT instances.

Title: Data analytics for maintenance with segmented customers in product-as-a-service environment
Authors: Ou Tang, Johan Vogt Duberg
Affiliations: Linköping University
Abstract: Original equipment manufacturers nowadays are shifting towards a product-as-a-service strategy; therefore, more responsibility for maintenance. Since maintenance decisions rely essentially on the product’s failure time affected by usage patterns, differentiating maintenance could potentially reduce failures and maintenance costs; however, it requires methods for identifying customer groups in datasets with mixed failure information. Therefore, to explore the underlying customer segments, this study introduces a mixed Weibull distribution which is defined as a linear combination of two distributions, each defined by its own Weibull density function. Because the higher-order moments of the mixed Weibull distribution can be expressed analytically, we derive closed-form expressions for the corresponding parameter estimates.
